metadata.title: AI Queueing Theory Foundations — Sources
metadata.description: Primary texts and references for 11 queueing-theory primitives: Little's Law, M/M/1, M/M/c (Erlang-C), M/G/1 P-K formula, priority queues, Jackson networks, Kingman's formula, bufferbloat, USL, Erlang-B loss systems, and fork-join queues.

foundational_texts.name: Queueing Systems, Vol. 1: Theory
foundational_texts.description: Kleinrock, L. (1975). Wiley-Interscience. The canonical reference for M/M/1, M/M/c, M/G/1, priority queues, and Jackson networks. Primary source for primitives 01–07.

foundational_texts.name: Queueing Systems, Vol. 2: Computer Applications
foundational_texts.description: Kleinrock, L. (1976). Wiley-Interscience. Application of queueing theory to computer systems, packet-switched networks, and scheduling. Primary source for primitives 05, 06, 08.

foundational_texts.name: Performance Modeling and Design of Computer Systems
foundational_texts.description: Harchol-Balter, M. (2013). Cambridge University Press. Rigorous treatment of M/M/1, M/M/c, M/G/1, priority queues, fork-join, and scheduling policies. Primary source for all 11 primitives.

foundational_texts.name: Introduction to Queueing Theory (2nd ed.)
foundational_texts.description: Cooper, R. B. (1981). North-Holland. Standard graduate text covering M/M/1, M/M/c, Erlang-B, Erlang-C, and networks of queues. Primary source for primitives 02, 03, 06, 10.

seminal_papers.name: SOAP: One Clean Analysis of All Age-Based Scheduling Policies
seminal_papers.description: Scully, Z., Harchol-Balter, M., & Scheller-Wolf, A. (2018). POMACS / ACM SIGMETRICS 2018. Unifying framework for all M/G/1 age-based scheduling policies (FCFS, FB, SRPT, Gittins, and variants). Provides a single response-time formula for any SOAP policy; primary theoretical basis for comparing SRPT, Gittins, and foreground-background scheduling.

seminal_papers.name: A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW
seminal_papers.description: Little, J. D. C. (1961). Operations Research, 9(3), 383–387. Formal proof of Little's Law. Primary source for primitive 01.

seminal_papers.name: Solution of some Problems in the Theory of Probabilities of Significance in Automatic Telephone Exchanges
seminal_papers.description: Erlang, A. K. (1917). Post Office Electrical Engineers' Journal, 10, 189–197. Original derivation of Erlang-B and Erlang-C formulas. Primary source for primitives 03, 10.

seminal_papers.name: Networks of Waiting Lines
seminal_papers.description: Jackson, J. R. (1957). Operations Research, 5(4), 518–521. Product-form solution for open networks of M/M/c queues. Primary source for primitive 06.

seminal_papers.name: The Single Server Queue in Heavy Traffic
seminal_papers.description: Kingman, J. F. C. (1961). Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society, 57(4), 902–904. Heavy-traffic approximation for G/G/1 queue wait time. Primary source for primitive 07.

seminal_papers.name: Über eine Aufgabe der Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie
seminal_papers.description: Pollaczek, F. (1930). Mathematische Zeitschrift, 32(1), 64–100. Original derivation of the P-K (Pollaczek-Khinchine) mean-value formula for M/G/1. Primary source for primitive 04.

seminal_papers.name: Mathematical theory of a stationary queue
seminal_papers.description: Khinchine, A. Y. (1932). Matematicheskii Sbornik, 39(4), 73–84. Independent derivation of the P-K formula. Co-primary source for primitive 04.

seminal_papers.name: The Approximate Analysis of Fork/Join Synchronization in Parallel Queues
seminal_papers.description: Nelson, R. & Tantawi, A. N. (1988). IEEE Transactions on Computers, 37(6), 739–743. Approximation analysis for fork-join queue response times. Primary source for primitive 11.

books_and_monographs.name: Guerrilla Capacity Planning
books_and_monographs.description: Gunther, N. J. (2007). Springer. Introduces the Universal Scalability Law (USL) including contention (σ) and coherency (κ) coefficients, retrograde scaling, and N_max. Primary source for primitive 09.

books_and_monographs.name: A General Theory of Computational Scalability Based on Rational Functions
books_and_monographs.description: Gunther, N. J. (2008). arXiv:0808.1431 (posted August 2008; corrected 2026-07-11 — prior entry had a stray 'cs/' prefix and mislabeled the year as 2007). Formal mathematical derivation of the USL model. Secondary source for primitive 09.

applied_references.name: Bufferbloat: Dark Buffers in the Internet
applied_references.description: Gettys, J. & Nichols, K. (2012). ACM Queue, 9(11). Coined and defined the bufferbloat phenomenon; motivation for AQM solutions. Primary source for primitive 08.

applied_references.name: Controlling Queue Delay (CoDel)
applied_references.description: Nichols, K. & Jacobson, V. (2012). ACM Queue, 10(5). CoDel (Controlled Delay) active queue management algorithm; solution for bufferbloat. Supporting source for primitive 08.

applied_references.name: Validity of the Single Processor Approach to Achieving Large Scale Computing Capabilities
applied_references.description: Amdahl, G. (1967). AFIPS, 30, 483–485. Original Amdahl's Law — parallel speedup with serialized fraction. Degenerate case of USL (κ=0). Supporting source for primitive 09.

applied_references.name: Approximations for the GI/G/m queue
applied_references.description: Whitt, W. (1993). Production and Operations Management, 2(2), 114–161. Heavy-traffic approximations for G/G/c (multi-server generalization of Kingman). Supporting source for primitive 07.

applied_references.name: MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters
applied_references.description: Dean, J. & Ghemawat, S. (2008). CACM, 51(1), 107–113. MapReduce architecture with speculative execution for straggler mitigation. Supporting source for primitive 11 (fork-join straggler handling).

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: A Gittins Policy for Optimizing Tail Latency
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Harlev, A., Yu, G., & Scully, Z. (2025). SIGMETRICS 2025 / POMACS. First scheduling policy achieving strong tail optimality in the light-tailed M/G/1 without known job sizes, using a Gittins index with a novel negative discount rate.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: Finite-Time Behavior of Erlang-C Model: Mixing Time, Mean Queue Length and Tail Bounds
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Nguyen, H. H., Varma, S. M., & Maguluri, S. T. (2025). SIGMETRICS 2025 / POMACS. First finite-time (non-asymptotic) bounds for the M/M/c / Erlang-C queue: mixing time, transient mean queue length, and tail bounds; phase transition at the Halfin-Whitt heavy-traffic regime.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: Queueing, Predictions, and Large Language Models: Challenges and Open Problems
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Mitzenmacher, M. & Shahout, R. (2025). Stochastic Systems, Vol. 15, No. 3. Peer-reviewed queueing framework for LLM inference scheduling: SPRPT with predicted output lengths, Trail policy (preemption age threshold for KV-cache cost avoidance), graceful degradation under bounded prediction error; open problems in memory-aware and compound LLM scheduling.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: Throughput-Optimal Scheduling Algorithms for LLM Inference and AI Agents
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Dai, J. G., Deng, T., Li, Y., & Peng, T. (2026). arXiv:2504.07347 v3 (May 2026). Fluid-limit framework for multi-class batched processing networks. Proves work-conserving scheduling achieves maximum throughput for single LLM inference engines and for DAG/fork-join multi-agent routing topologies; shows work-conservation alone is insufficient for general multi-agent networks with batch-size constraints or cyclic routing. Empirically validates Orca and Sarathi-serve as throughput-optimal; identifies vanilla vLLM and FasterTransformer as lacking maximum stability. CORRECTION 2026-08-14: a prior entry wrongly merged this paper with DOI 10.1145/3771574 and the title 'Optimal Scheduling Algorithms for LLM Inference: Theory and Practice'. That is a separate paper (see BariHegdeDeVeciana2026); this one retains its original title and remains a preprint.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: Optimal Scheduling Algorithms for LLM Inference: Theory and Practice
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Bari, A., Hegde, P., & de Veciana, G. (2026). POMACS Vol. 9, No. 3, Article 59 / SIGMETRICS 2026 (DOI 10.1145/3771574; conference abstract DOI 10.1145/3801489.3806878). Identifies optimal tiling and dynamic resource allocation as the binding design principles for prefill/decode scheduling. Introduces the Resource-Aware Dynamic (RAD) scheduler, proven throughput-optimal under mild conditions, and the SLO-Aware LLM Inference (SLAI) scheduler which prioritizes decode requests near their TBT deadline and reorders prefill by prompt length. Reports 53% median TTFT reduction and 26% higher maximum serving capacity vs. Sarathi-serve.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: On the Distribution of Sojourn Times in Tandem Queues
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Ciucu, F. & Mehri, S. (2025). POMACS / SIGMETRICS 2025, Vol. 9, No. 2, Article 27. Polynomial-exponential bounds on end-to-end sojourn time distributions in tandem queues with general arrivals and light-tailed service; bounds are numerically sharp for two-stage exponential case; polynomial degree tracks number of bottleneck stages.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: Robust Gittins for Stochastic Scheduling
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Moseley, B., Newman, H., Pruhs, K., & Zhou, R. (2025). SIGMETRICS 2025. Proves standard Gittins index is not robust under distributional perturbation; introduces Robust Gittins policy with bounded degradation parameterized by a new distributional error measure.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: SageServe: Optimizing LLM Serving on Cloud Data Centers with Forecast Aware Auto-Scaling
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Jaiswal, S. et al. (2025/2026). POMACS / SIGMETRICS 2026. Multi-timescale queueing control for LLM cloud serving: short-horizon routing + long-horizon GPU VM scaling co-optimized via traffic forecasting and ILP. Production-validated at Microsoft Office 365 (10M+ requests/day, 3 regions). 25% GPU-hour savings, 80% reduction in autoscaling waste.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: Don't Stop Me Now: Embedding Based Scheduling for LLMs
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Shahout, R., Malach, E., Liu, C., Jiang, W., Yu, M., & Mitzenmacher, M. (2025). ICLR 2025 (Singapore, April 2025); preprint arXiv:2410.01035. Venue confirmed 2026-08-14 (was previously recorded as pending). Introduces TRAIL: recycles the target LLM's own per-token internal embedding into a lightweight classifier predicting each running request's remaining output length, then applies a prediction-based SRPT variant with limited preemption — preemption allowed early while KV-cache footprint is small, restricted as requests near completion.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: Outperforming Multiserver SRPT at All Loads
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Grosof, I. & Hurtado-Lange, D. (2025/2026). Accepted SIGMETRICS 2026. Introduces SEK-SMOD, the first scheduling policy to provably achieve lower mean response time than SRPT-k across all loads and all job size distributions in M/G/k queues. Preprint under peer review.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: A Queueing-Theoretic Framework for Stability Analysis of LLM Inference with KV Cache Memory Constraints
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Nie, C., Si, N., & Zhou, Z. (2026). ICML 2026; arXiv:2605.04595 (May 2026). First queueing-theoretic framework incorporating BOTH computation and GPU memory constraints into LLM inference stability analysis. Derives rigorous stability and instability conditions for whether a service can absorb its arrival rate without unbounded queue growth, under continuous batching and any work-conserving scheduling policy. Yields a cluster-sizing tool: combine forecast arrival rate with the derived stable service rate. Validated on production GPU environments with stability-condition deviations typically within 10%.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: Service-Induced Congestion in Memory-Constrained LLM Serving
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Ao, R., Dong, J., Luo, G., & Simchi-Levi, D. (2026). arXiv:2606.15555 (June 2026). Identifies service-induced congestion: KV cache grows per generated token, so serving itself creates endogenous future capacity pressure; exceeding memory forces eviction and restart of active requests. Proves the eviction-free equilibrium is UNSTABLE for homogeneous saturated workloads, converging to a limit cycle with up to 50% throughput loss. For heterogeneous workloads, establishes stability criteria showing heterogeneity desynchronizes completions and stabilizes the system; under input-dominated scaling, coprime decode lengths stabilize while synchronized completions drive instability. Preprint.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: A Tale of Two Traffics: Optimizing Tail Latency in the Light-Tailed M/G/k
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Yu, G., Harlev, A., Adakroy, R., & Scully, Z. (2026). POMACS / SIGMETRICS 2026. Proves gamma-Boost is tail-constant optimal for the light-tailed M/G/k in heavy traffic, but shows empirically it can underperform FCFS at lighter loads. Introduces an improved variant that counterintuitively gives MORE priority to larger jobs, proven heavy-traffic optimal with state-of-the-art empirical tail latency at light load. Practical implication: tail-latency policy choice is load-regime-dependent, so a policy tuned at peak may be harmful off-peak.

recent_papers_2025_2026.name: inference-fleet-sim: A Queueing-Theory-Grounded Fleet Capacity Planner for LLM Inference
recent_papers_2025_2026.description: Chen, H., Liu, X., Liu, Y., Jiang, J., He, B., & Liu, X. (2026). arXiv:2603.16054. Combines analytical M/G/c queueing theory with discrete-event simulation for GPU fleet sizing under heavy-tailed token-length distributions. Demonstrates that analytical M/G/c alone produces incorrect fleet sizing for split thresholds, GPU type selection, and utilization assessment under realistic LLM workloads.
